content.text: lost a rook endgame i think was drawn. me: K g6, R a1, pawn none. him: K e5, R h2, pawn f4. my move, i played Ra5+ and he walked his king up and pushed. was it drawn

With your king already on g6 in front of the f-pawn's path (f5/f6 squares nearby), this type of position is usually a **draw** if you keep your king close and your rook active. A rook vs. rook+one pawn ending where the defending king controls the queening path is the classic drawing setup.

What went wrong is probably the *plan* after Ra5+: checking from the side lets the king approach the rook and escape the checks. Typical defensive ideas:

- **Philidor-style**: keep your rook on the 6th rank (here, from your side, the rank in front of the pawn) to stop the king advancing, and only go to long-distance checks from behind once the pawn advances.
- **Checks from behind** the pawn (Rf1) are often strongest: the rook on f1 attacks the pawn and the king can't hide from checks along the file easily.

Without the exact position on a board I can't give the precise drawing move, but Rf1 (attacking f4 from behind) is the natural candidate to check with an engine.
engine says Rf1 draws lol. Ra5+ was -3

That's the classic lesson: in rook endgames, a rook *behind* the passed pawn is usually best, whether you're attacking or defending. Lucena and Philidor positions are worth learning properly; they come up more than any opening line.
